key_discoveries.title: True Belief Failure is Heuristic-Based
key_discoveries.summary: TB fails (40%) because model defaults to first-mentioned location. Adding 'Alice now believes X' fixes it to 88% (p=0.0015).
key_discoveries.implication: ToM capability EXISTS but is obscured by surface heuristics.

key_discoveries.title: First-Mention Circuit Identified
key_discoveries.summary: Heads L23H4 (103x), L13H10 (232x) strongly attend to first-mentioned location.
key_discoveries.implication: Targeted ablation could reveal genuine ToM without prompt engineering.

key_discoveries.title: Multi-Agent is Easier Than Single-Agent
key_discoveries.summary: Multi-agent scenarios achieve 100% accuracy vs 40% for single-agent TB.
key_discoveries.implication: Model handles multiple entities better than belief updates.

key_discoveries.title: Two Distinct Social Circuits
key_discoveries.summary: ToM heads (L32-34) track agents. First-mention heads (L13, L23, L31) track locations.
key_discoveries.implication: Social cognition has modular architecture in LLMs.

key_discoveries.title: Peak Belief Processing at L28
key_discoveries.summary: Layer 28 shows maximum belief discriminability (10.94), not earlier layers.
key_discoveries.implication: Belief decisions form late in the network.

mats_summary.title: Collaboration Circuits: Mechanistic Interpretability of Multi-Agent ToM
mats_summary.key_claim: LLMs have ToM capability obscured by first-mention heuristics
implications: Heuristics may interfere with genuine reasoning
